description: Range test of the Demazure/reduction-length route to a categorical decay rate. With N_ops = q_0^L and q_0 pinned, L is determined (fit-free): 34.5 (Z) to 598.0 (neutron). The corpus assigns a nucleon B_3, so l(w_0) = 3 — short by ~199x. The order-zero single-braid reading FAILS. The required depths (n >= 9/24/29/36) are tower depths, consistent in form with the 2026-09-03 full-tower ruling but not evidence for it. The neutron's L = 598.0027 is NOT a near-integer result: the offset is inside the PDG lifetime band.
q0AnchorReason: AGENTS.md 2026-08-07 owner directive: proton is the default

data.identity: N_ops = q_0^L  =>  L = ln(N_ops)/ln(q_0), q_0 pinned, no fit
data.scope: (a). Excludes a reduction length OF THE PARTICLE'S OWN BRAID as the carrier. Does NOT exclude a tower-level length, a different incompleteness measure, or a non-exponential dependence.
data.open: whether any Demazure incompleteness measure at tower depth n ~ 9-36 reproduces the ordering Z < tau < pion < muon < neutron. Nothing here derives it.

assertions.name: length_exponent_is_fit_free
assertions.detail: q_0 is pinned, so L = ln(N_ops)/ln(q_0) is read off rather than adjusted — there is no parameter to tune

assertions.name: order_zero_single_braid_reading_FAILS
assertions.detail: the neutron needs L = 598.0027 and its corpus braid B_3 caps l(w_0) at 3 — short by 199.33x. No w inside S_3 can help; 3 is the ceiling. A decay rate is NOT a reduction length of the particle's own braid.

assertions.name: required_depths_are_tower_not_strand_counts
assertions.detail: n >= 9 (Z), 24 (tau), 29 (muon), 36 (neutron) — depths in H_n, not the particles' strand counts. Consistent in FORM with the 2026-09-03 full-tower ruling; consistency in form is NOT evidence, and nothing here derives these depths or their ordering

assertions.name: the_neutron_near_integer_is_NOT_a_result
assertions.detail: L = 598.002698 sits 0.002698 from 598, inside the PDG bottle band (0.005455) and far inside the beam-bottle spread (0.08729). One coincidence in five samples; the other four are not near integers.
